## Why

I chose a solitary figure of a priest, represented through the recognizable form of a man in full priestly vestments (cassock, alb, stole, and chasuble), specifically in the act of raising his right hand in the gesture of absolution, to symbolize *Perpensis circumstantiis*. This document addresses the need for absolution in exceptional circumstances where clergy have fled, and the specific gesture directly visually translates the extended "faculties to absolve" granted by the Pope. The figure stands alone, reflecting both the isolation of faithful priests and the universal nature of the Church's sacramental power, which is no longer confined by the original geographic restrictions; abstraction was rejected because a clear, single figure is the most direct way to represent this specific, human-centered sacramental action that Pius VI is authorizing.

## Image

A high-end 3D sculptural render, centered and isolated on a transparent background, depicting a single, recognizable figure of a Catholic priest in a profound moment of absolution. The sculpture, rendered in a blend of cast bronze with verdigris patina and polished gold details on the priestly vestments, stands full-height on a simple, dark, unadorned circular plinth, positioned dead-center in the frame with generous transparent negative space surrounding it. The figure is a man of middle age, looking forward with a serious, compassionate expression, his face carved with realistic detail. He wears traditional late 18th-century priestly attire: a dark bronze cassock, a patterned alb (white-patinaed bronze) showing intricate lacework, a long stole (gold-patinaed with stylized cross patterns), and a matching chasuble (dark gold and deep green bronze). His right hand is raised, palm forward, fingers extended in the recognizable, universal gesture of the Sign of the Cross for absolution. The gesture is clear and emphatic. His left hand is held close to his chest, perhaps clasping a small, simple crucifix. The sculpture exhibits a luxury sacred-object finish, with realistic physically based materials, global illumination, ray-traced reflections on the gold, pronounced ambient occlusion in the fabric folds, and subtle micro-surface textures like imperfections and tool marks. The lighting is dramatic and high-contrast, with a strong key light from the above-front-left carving the form in sharp chiaroscuro, a subtle fill light from the front-right preserving readability, and a pronounced rim light from the rear-right defining the silhouette against the transparent void. The camera angle is frontal, orthographic, at mid-height, with an 85mm lens equivalent and f/8 aperture, ensuring symmetrical composition and no perspective distortion. The sculpture is perfectly isolated, suitable for compositing, with no environmental elements or readable text.

I have reviewed the generated sculpture against the theological and technical constraints. The selection of a priest in chasuble to symbolize the expansion of faculties is highly appropriate and instantly recognizable. The technical execution is flawless, adhering strictly to the orthographic perspective and high-contrast lighting requirements. The materials are rendered with premium quality, and the background is transparent as requested. I will show the image to the user.
